note: Content source for the Plan & Progress page. Edit this; ask Claude Design to refresh the design from it. SCOPE RULE: this page carries exactly one live milestone in detail, plus an archive of completed ones. Future milestones live in Roadmap & Backlog and are not duplicated here — a plan written three milestones ahead is a guess wearing a schedule. When a milestone completes it moves into `archive` with its decisions intact, and the next milestone's plan is written then, informed by what the last one taught. `status` is DONE | NOW | LATER and drives tile colour, pill and sidebar dot. `activities[]` renders the work table; `notes[]` renders the decision log inside the milestone. A milestone or phase may carry `statusNote` — HTML shown as a hover card on its status pill, using the same gloss-card mechanism as the System Design page. Use it when a status is true but incomplete.

site.title: Plan & Progress
site.lede: One milestone at a time, in detail. Everything after it lives in the Roadmap; everything before it is archived here, decisions intact.
site.footerNote: Plan · the live milestone and the archive of completed work for aiml-signal-system. Public-safe.

currentStatus.body: The repo is public at github.com/varun-sridharan/aiml-signal-system and the Framer runs end to end with a gated eval harness. The system is pivoting. The AI Weekly News Digest — a scheduled cloud task that has run for weeks — knows what to say, has 91 tiered sources and a reader. This system knows how to prove what it says is true, and has no reader at all. The two are converging into one hosted product, and the Digest is retired once the new one has run clean for two to three weeks. Now building M1: Reader and Framer on Railway, both gated, producing the weekly debrief at a URL.

howItWorks: One live milestone: this page details the milestone being built now. Later milestones are in Roadmap & Backlog with exit criteria but no task breakdown.
Binary exit criteria: a milestone is done when every criterion is observably true, not when the activities are ticked off.
Plans are written late on purpose: M2's detailed plan is written when M1 completes. Slipped items and newly discovered work land in the Roadmap first, then in the next plan.
Activities say what and why; the how lives in a canonical prompt under prompts/.
Notes = decision log: decisions, tradeoffs and what was rejected, recorded per milestone as it is built.
Content vs design: every document is JSON content rendered by a design from Claude Design. Claude edits the JSON; the HTML is generated and never hand-edited.

phases.title: Reading and writing, hosted
phases.endState: Reader and Framer running on Railway with no local dependency, both gated, producing the weekly debrief at a URL. Exit is binary: the canonicalisation gate is green including a planted duplicate; the faithfulness and structural gates are green on a golden week including a planted fabrication; the Weekly Digest tab renders the debrief; thumbs are captured.
phases.why: The first milestone that is a system rather than a store. Reader alone fills a database nobody can see, and a milestone whose exit criterion is invisible is a weak one. Two agents, two gates, one page.

activities.outcome: App, Postgres and scheduler live at a URL; the existing pages serve from it with zero local dependency
activities.why: Everything else in this milestone assumes a host. It also dissolves the constraint the old Digest was designed around — that a scheduled run cannot write to its own page

activities.outcome: agents/budget.py and agents/llm.py, with the breaker upgraded to stop-before
activities.why: Reader is the breaker's second caller. Extract at the second use — not the first, which is premature, and not the third, by which point there are copies to keep in sync

activities.activity: Storage layer, with the excerpt rule
activities.outcome: Postgres for items, sources, the interest graph, runs and feedback; blob storage for fetched excerpts, written once at fetch time and never re-fetched
activities.why: The faithfulness gate compares a quoted span against the stored excerpt. Re-fetch at grade time and a publisher's edit turns the gate red for no reason — the same class of problem as a model alias moving under a pinned test

activities.outcome: Canonicalisation, dedup, provenance and corroboration; seeded with the Digest's 91 tiered domains; /add-news fetches immediately
activities.why: Two agents whose steps are fixed and whose work is mostly deterministic. Merging them removes a handoff that bought nothing

activities.outcome: A golden URL set with a planted near-duplicate (hard gate, free) and hand labels for corroboration; the miss ledger opens
activities.why: Canonicalisation is code answering a code question, so it gates at zero cost. The miss ledger tracks time-to-close, not count — unknown unknowns stay unknown, but a domain handed over twice is a visible failure

activities.activity: Port the Framer and its gate, unchanged
activities.outcome: The Framer writes Learning for the Week and This Week's Stories on the hosted system; the existing golden cases run against it
activities.why: Port it, do not extend it. Moving a component and changing it at the same time means a red run cannot be attributed to either. The two-call fix and usefulness calibration are separate, later work

activities.outcome: Two subsections — Learning for the Week, This Week's Stories — with thumbs up and down, and a free-form box on thumbs-down
activities.why: The first real label this system has ever had. The usefulness rubric has been reported and never gated because there was nothing to calibrate it against

notes: Cadence is a decision, not a default. A daily brief optimises for missing nothing, and what it produces is a queue — which is why the previous daily digest was retired despite working as designed. Monthly is too slow for a field that moves weekly. The two clocks are separate: ingestion runs continuously because it is deterministic and costs almost nothing, while judgement runs weekly because judgement is what costs money.

Event triggers, honestly. Webhooks effectively do not exist in this space. /add-news is the one genuinely event-driven path and fetches on arrival. Feeds are the closest thing to an event source for the tiered domains, and a weekly crawl covers the rest.

Practice and Control Hub are off the navigation until their milestones. Half-built surfaces with a soon badge on one page and real content on another is worse than absence — that inconsistency was live on the site and is the reason for the rule. Their files stay in the repository; they are simply not linked.

crossCutting.title: Cross-cutting infrastructure
crossCutting.note: A trajectory, not a single milestone.
items: Data layer: JSON files today → Postgres at M1, because Railway containers restart and memory loses everything. pgvector and multi-tenant sessions only if this is ever productised. The user_id field has been carried from the first commit for exactly that reason.
Excerpt store: immutable, written once at fetch time. This is what makes the faithfulness gate reproducible — it is infrastructure, not a detail.
Observability: usage.json becomes a structured per-run trace at M1, and a real observability tool if run volume justifies one.
Cost: ledger and breaker exist; the breaker becomes stop-before at M1, when a second agent starts spending.

items.title: Build & prove the Framer
items.endState: a Framer agent that turns data/evals/golden/reference_2026-08-04.json into a brief matching the Bento reference voice.
items.why: Framer quality is the riskiest assumption in the system — if the voice lands, the whole thing is worth building; it's the cheapest bet to de-risk first.

activities.activity: Finalize the Framer build prompt (+ Evals)
activities.outcome: Canonical prompt with faithfulness/usefulness graders baked in
activities.why: Reproducible recipe; evals from day one

activities.activity: Generate the Framer agent via Claude Code

activities.outcome: You judge whether the voice sounds right
activities.why: The go / no-go on the whole system
activities.prompt: — your taste is the gate

notes: Locked Framer rules: worked examples on AI items only; synthesis "thread" required; DO THIS reserved for AI; reading-time header; inline connections.
Faithfulness = hard zero-hallucination gate (objective); usefulness = soft, learned target (subjective).
Test against application/Signal.html, not vibes.
Done 2026-08-09 (commit df8adfd, Opus 5): Framer built & run — 7 items, 2 DO THIS, ~5 min read, $0.10. Batched to 2 calls (Opus framing + Haiku check) with prompt caching + cost breaker, all working.

Voice verdict = GO: thread carries a real correlation + contradiction and reaches its own conclusion; connections genuine. Two weak spots to tune later: iStar example clause doesn't parse; Kimi K3 example vaguer than the reference's concrete "~1/10th cost".

Key finding → Phase 3: the faithfulness check produced a false positive (flagged $965B as unsupported though it was in the excerpt). Two grader bugs: it missed a clause, and it graded thread/headline text against a single item's excerpt. The grader needs its own eval; the thread must be checked against the union of excerpts.
Deviations, both fine: built the prompt file fresh (option 3, no invented Scout list); switched the framing call to streaming after the SDK blocked a 24k-token non-streaming request (no spend).

items.title: Framer eval harness (golden set)
items.endState: a tiny offline eval that scores the Framer (faithfulness assertion + usefulness rubric) against 1–2 labeled days.
items.why: turns "is the voice right?" from a vibe into a number, and makes every future prompt tweak safe via regression.

activities.activity: Build a golden set from labeled days

activities.outcome: Grader rewritten: claim ledger with quoted spans, correct scope, code-verified evidence

activities.why: Safe iteration on the Framer prompt

notes: Eval harness lives in the repo from early on; the Tuner-driven learning matures later (needs weeks of data).
Held-out slice kept separate from anything the Tuner adapts on (train/test hygiene).
First golden-set case comes free: the Phase 2 grader false positive. Fix the check to (a) not miss clauses and (b) grade the thread against the union of all item excerpts, not one item's.

Done 2026-08-19 (Opus 5): run_evals.py runs three checks — faithfulness (hard gate, 1 Haiku call), structural assertions (hard gate, free), usefulness rubric (soft, reported). Both seeded regressions pass; run costs ~$0.02.

The grader's real bug was scope, not carelessness. It was shown the excerpt first and the writing second, so it enumerated the excerpt's claims and never checked the framing at all — which is why $965B "failed" and why fabricated facts sailed through. Writing now comes first in the payload, the excerpt is labelled ground truth, and each claim must carry a verbatim span.
Second false positive found while labelling: the 2026-08-13 re-run flagged "~80% of Q1 dollars", which the excerpt states word for word. Seeded as a second regression case.

Two extras beyond the brief, both earned by a failing test: a code check that every quoted span is literally in the excerpt (a grader can invent a citation; a substring match can't), and temperature=0 on the grader — at default sampling it disagreed with itself on ~1 run in 3, which would have failed builds at random. 5/5 clean runs after.

Known limit, carried to Phase 8: the gate is deterministic per input, but on unseen days the grader still sometimes enumerates an inference as a claim. Fine for regression (the golden day is fixed); revisit before the grader guards live briefs — likely by moving it to a stronger model.
Usefulness stays ungated until calibrated against your own ratings. Judge runs on Haiku to keep spend low; upgrade it the day it starts gating.

Reopened 2026-09-15. A second golden case, golden/negative-01/, was added to test the direction the suite could not test: every unit until now expected expected_unsupported: [], so a grader that flagged nothing passed everything. On its first run the new case failed, and re-running both cases five times each measured the grader rather than guessing at it. 2026-08-04: 18 false positives, identical in all five runs — every one an implication, recommendation or worked-example scenario, which the grader's own prompt names as never-enumerate. negative-01: the planted distortion (“raised $965B” where the source says “valued at $965B”) was caught in 2 of 5 runs; in the other 3 the grader enumerated the source's sentences instead of the writing's — the same scope bug this phase closed, returning on the first case it had not been tested against. Ruled out: model drift (one snapshot, the alias never moved), sampling noise (byte-identical 5/5 on the clean case), mis-wired inputs (verified: framing_from_framed_day(case[“output”])), and wrong labels (they match the prompt's own rules). The harness itself is sound and did its job — the grader it grades is not. Numbers in data/evals/baseline-2026-09-15.md. Status left at DONE because the deliverable of this phase is the harness, and the harness is what found this.

Half closed 2026-09-15. The Framer now splits every field into fact and interpretation runs and only the fact runs reach the grader. False positives on the clean day went 18 → 0, identical across three runs, with grader errors 1 → 0 and output 2253 → 1309 tokens. That half is fixed structurally — the flagged clauses are no longer sent, so they cannot be flagged however the grader behaves. The other half is not: negative-01 caught the plant 2 of 3, against 2 of 5 before, which establishes nothing at that n — and the split was never aimed at it. The miss is the grader reading the source's sentences instead of the writing's, which a facts-only payload does not address. Numbers in data/evals/result-2026-09-15-split.md.
items.statusNote: Done, with one issue open and scheduled. The faithfulness gate passes on the clean day — false positives went 18 → 0, identical across three runs, once the Framer began splitting its output into checkable claims and its own reading, and only the claims were sent to the grader. What is still open: on a case with a fabrication planted on purpose, the grader misses it roughly one run in three. The source says “Anthropic is valued at $965B”; the brief says “Anthropic raised $965B”. In the miss, the grader enumerates the source's sentence instead of the brief's, quotes it as its own evidence, and returns supported at confidence 1.0 — so the distortion is never examined. That is the dangerous direction: a false positive is loud and costs a good sentence, this is silent and reaches the reader. The fix, scheduled for Phase 6: split grading into two calls. The first enumerates claims with the excerpt withheld entirely, so there is nothing to copy from; the second judges that list against the excerpt. Structural rather than instructional — the prompt already forbids this in plain language and it happens anyway. lifted_claims already detects the behaviour deterministically (zero firings in 75 claims on the clean day) and becomes a regression detector once the fix lands.
